title: Rodent Behavioral Testing to Assess Functional Deficits Caused by Microelectrode Implantation in the Rat Motor Cortex
protocol: Anesthetize the animal in an induction chamber using isoflurane (2 - 4%).
Monitor the animal’s heart rate and blood-oxygen content continuously during anesthesia.
Move the animal to a nose cone for continued anesthesia administration.
Subcutaneously inject cefazolin (25 mg/kg) to prevent infection.
Inject carprofen (5 mg/kg) subcutaneously to manage pain.
Apply ophthalmic ointment to the animal's eyes to prevent drying.
Trim the animal’s toenails using small animal nail clippers to prevent scratching of sutures.
Shave the animal’s head thoroughly from behind the ears to between the eyes using an electric razor trimmer.
Provide a local analgesia with an SQ injection of bupivacaine (0.3 mL of 0.125% bupivacaine diluted from stock solution) at the top of the animal's head in the area of the incision.
Mount the animal on a stereotaxic frame, using ear bars to keep the head from moving during the surgery.
Place a circulating water heating pad under the animal to maintain the animal's internal temperature.
Apply a sterile drape, e.g., institutionally-approved sterile plastic wrap, to isolate the surgical field.
Scrub the surgical area using an alternating betadine solution and isopropanol scrubs.
Perform a toe pinch according to the institutional protocol to ensure the animal is under the surgical plane.
Create an incision of approximately 1 inch down midline exposing the skull using a No. 10 scalpel blade.
Bluntly remove the periosteum using a cotton-tipped applicator, and stop any bleeding using a gauze pad.
Retract the surrounding tissue using alligator clips.
Clean and dehydrate the skull with hydrogen peroxide.
Place a few drops of cyanoacrylate-based tissue adhesive on the exposed skull to improve the dental cement bonding in later steps.
Mark the region of the motor cortex corresponding to forepaw movement approximately 3 mm lateral to midline and 2 mm anterior to bregma by creating a nick in the bone.
Remove a portion of the skull using a 1.75-mm rounded tip dental drill intermittently.
Reflect the dura using a fine hooked 45° dura pick.
Clean any bleeding using a cotton-tipped applicator and saline, taking care not to directly touch the brain surface.
Carefully mount the sterilized microelectrode in the universal holder on the stereotaxic frame.
Ensure that the headstage interface connector of the electrode is firmly held by the holder.
Position the tip of the electrode over the open craniotomy using micromanipulators.
Gently lower the electrode approximately 2 mm into the brain using the micromanipulators as a measurement guide.
Take caution to avoid any visible vasculature whenever possible.
Carefully release the connector from the universal holder and retract the insertion arm.
Clean any bleeding from around the electrode using a cotton-tipped applicator and saline.
Seal off the craniotomy around the implanted electrode using a silicone elastomer.
Fix the electrode to the skull using dental cement.
Bring the edges of the incision together at the front and back of the cement headcap and suture them shut.
Allow the animal to recover on a circulating water heating pad while continuing to monitor its vital signs.
Provide animals with SQ cephalosporin antibiotic (25 mg/kg) during post-operative days 1 - 3.
Provide animals with a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory (5 mg/kg) during post-operative days 1 - 3.
Monitor the animals daily for signs of pain or discomfort, bleeding, weight change, or suture issues through at least post-operative day 5.
Test the animals 2x per test in the week prior to electrode implantation surgery.
Calculate pre-surgery baseline scores from behavioral tests.
Allow animals to rest for 1 week following the surgery.
Begin behavior testing 2x per week on each test after resting period.
Clean all testing equipment with a chlorine dioxide-based sterilant at the beginning of each session.
Sterilize testing equipment again after each animal is tested.
Film the open field grid and ladder testing sessions.
Use a video camera (1080p, minimum of 15 fps, 78° diagonal field of view) for filming.
Bring animals to the testing room before each testing day.
Allow animals to acclimate in the testing room for at least 20 min.
Ensure the testing room is light and temperature-controlled.
Use consistent personnel to complete all behavioral tests.
Store video data from the testing sessions on a laptop.
Provide food rewards such as cereals, banana chips, or crackers during training.
Normalize weekly testing performances to pre-surgery scores for each animal.
Place the animal in the center of the open field grid facing away from the tester.
Allow the animal to run freely for 3 min while recording a video.
Remove the animal from the grid after completion and return it to the cage.
Clean the grid thoroughly with chlorine dioxide-based sterilant.
Analyze the number of gridlines crossed, total distance traveled, and maximum velocity using video tracking software.
Move the animal to a temporary clean holding cage to begin ladder testing.
Set up the ladder so that it bridges two cages, with one end resting on a clean cage and the other on the animal's home cage.
Position a video camera at the center of the ladder at rung height to capture the entire ladder.
Hold the animal to the starting line of the ladder, allowing their front paws to touch the first rung.
Allow the animal to cross the ladder at their own pace.
Record the time elapsed from when the animal's paw touches the first rung until reaching the finish line at the third-to-last rung.
Assign a penalty score if the animal turns around or does not move for 20 seconds.
Allow each animal to cross the ladder 5 times per testing day with approximately 1 minute rest in between each run.
Average the fastest 3 runs per day as a metric of fine motor function.
Record the number of times each front paw slips off the rungs using video tracking software.
Calibrate the grip strength meter before each testing session.
Measure the grip strength in grams by positioning the meter on the edge of a counter with handlebars extended over the floor.
Hold the animal by the base of the tail and allow it to grab the handlebars with both front paws.
Pull the animal away from the meter by the base of the tail with slow, steady force.
Record the maximum grip strength exerted by the animal as displayed on the digital output.
Test each animal 3 times per testing day with approximately 2 minutes rest in between each test.
Average the maximum grip strength output from each of the 3 trials as a metric of fine motor function.
Anesthetize animals deeply using ketamine (160 mg/kg) and xylazine (20 mg/kg).
Transcardially perfuse anesthetized animals.
Harvest brains from perfused animals.
Cryo-slice harvested brain tissue.
Stain tissue using immunohistochemical markers.
Quantify cellular response around the site of implantation.
Analyze behavioral performance in the open field grid at each weekly time point.
Analyze behavioral performance on the ladder at each weekly time point.
Analyze behavioral performance in grip strength testing at each weekly time point.
Compare control vs. implanted groups using a two-sample t-test for each test.
Quantify longitudinal performance using a mixed effect linear model.
Use ANOVA to determine factor effects with a significance level of p < 0.05.
Compare ladder performance with immunoglobin G (IgG) intensity.
Perform linear regression analysis between ladder performance and IgG intensity.
Calculate the correlation coefficient by Pearson's method.
